aiSummary: Speckled trout are the standout species across Choctawhatchee Bay right now, with quality fish being reported along with bull redfish and cruising tarpon in the broader area — the bite window is early morning before the summer heat peaks. Today's near-calm westerly winds and a strong waxing gibbous tidal push set up favorable conditions on the flats, but plan to wrap up by midday given the 14% storm chance before 1 PM and a brutal heat index near 106°F. The low tide falling around 2:39 PM will concentrate fish in deeper holes and channel edges through the afternoon for anyone willing to push past the heat.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel where bait gets pushed through on both tides. Pilings hold trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum year-round, with the lee-side pilings serving as the prime ambush zone on incoming tides. This is open, exposed water — it's typically the first spot to become unfishable when wind picks up.
bridge.todaysCall: With winds running W at 0–10 mph today, chop should be minimal and the bridge will be fishable throughout the early window — make the most of it before the heat becomes oppressive. The strong spring tide from the waxing gibbous moon means bait will be moving hard through the funnel; work the lee-side pilings as the tide drops toward the 2:39 PM low, concentrating fish against the structure. Trout and redfish are the realistic targets given current bay-wide reports, though sheepshead and black drum are always possible around the pilings. Slightly stained water and bright sun favor darker soft plastics or shrimp fished tight to structure. Be off the water or sheltered by noon with the storm window closing before 1 PM.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, plus trout and flounder near the mouth. Oyster bars at the creek mouth are the prime structure, and tree cover keeps it a few degrees cooler than the open bay while also providing shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions toward brackish territory where bass show up alongside small reds.
alaqua.todaysCall: The tree-lined banks make Alaqua a smart choice on a bright, high-heat day like today — shade and protection will help fish stay comfortable and active longer than on exposed flats. With the tide running out toward the 2:39 PM low, work the oyster bars at the mouth early as water drains off the adjacent grass and funnels baitfish through that zone. Redfish are the primary target here and align well with current bay-wide reports of solid reds being landed; trout are a legitimate secondary option near the mouth. Slightly stained water calls for noisy or high-contrast lures — a gold spoon or chartreuse paddle tail will help fish locate the bait. The protected nature of this bayou also makes it a reasonable safe harbor if that sub-14% storm chance materializes before 1 PM.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less fishing pressure than Alaqua and LaGrange, which generally means less-educated fish and a better shot at quality sight-fishing. Interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano occasionally work the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It offers less weather protection than LaGrange when conditions build.
basin.todaysCall: Lower pressure and interior grass flats make Basin Bayou a solid pick for sight-fishing redfish early this morning while light and wind are both minimal. The near-calm westerly forecast and strong tidal push from the spring tide phase will move bait across those shallow grass flats — get there at first light and work the edges as water begins dropping toward the afternoon low. Slightly stained water limits visibility some, but poling or drifting quietly in under two feet and watching for tailing or waking fish is still very doable. Speckled trout are a secondary option, consistent with bay-wide reports, especially near any deeper grass edges. Keep an eye on the sky and plan to exit before 1 PM given the storm window, since Basin offers less protection than nearby alternatives if weather builds.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is a top trout producer in this area — the oyster bars at the mouth are legendary, interior grass flats hold redfish year-round, and deep holes inside hold black drum and sheepshead. It is the most protected water on this side of the bay, making it the preferred refuge when weather builds. Expect consistent pressure but consistently consistent production.
lagrange.todaysCall: LaGrange earns its reputation on days like today — the protection it offers matters when a storm window exists before 1 PM, and you can fish confidently here knowing you have an exit plan if skies turn. Hit the oyster bars at the mouth during the early falling tide while the spring tide moon still has water moving briskly; trout stacked on those bars are the primary target and directly align with this week's bay-wide reports of plentiful specks. As the tide drops toward the 2:39 PM low, transition inside to the deeper holes where black drum and sheepshead become more accessible. Slightly stained water and bright sun suggest working the shadow lines near the oyster structure with a live shrimp or natural-colored soft plastic. Redfish on the interior flats are a consistent option throughout the morning as well.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a short tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, making it one of the most convenient and protected fisheries on this dashboard. Tidal flow pushes baitfish up the creek on incoming tides, concentrating redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges. The creek mouth is a prime flounder zone, and the upper section transitions to brackish water where bass mix with small reds.
fourmile.todaysCall: Four Mile Creek's short run from Shipyard Marina and its sheltered nature make it an efficient choice on a day with a storm window before 1 PM — you can launch, fish, and return quickly if conditions deteriorate. The tide is falling all morning toward the 2:39 PM low, so focus on the bends and grass edges where redfish and trout will stack as water drains out of the creek; the strong spring tide pull will make that bait-concentration effect pronounced today. The creek mouth is worth a few casts for flounder, though no specific flounder reports are circulating this week — it remains a structural inevitability regardless. Slightly stained water and calm winds mean finesse presentations in natural colors will work well in the low-flow upper sections, while a popping cork near the mouth can cover water efficiently. This is the safest pick on the dashboard if you want to be conservative about weather exposure.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide spot and one of the most productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay, with summer mornings being peak season for trout stacked on grass in two to four feet of water. Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides, adding a bonus target when current is running. It sits further from the 331 Bridge area than other bayous, so factor in run time when planning your day.
hogtown.todaysCall: Hogtown is directly in the wheelhouse of this week's bay-wide reports — speckled trout plentiful across the bay, and this is one of the bay's premier trout flats, with summer mornings being the historically proven peak window. Get here at or just after first light with the 5:57 AM sunrise and work the grass in two to four feet; the spring tide tidal push will have bait moving and trout actively feeding before the bright sun climbs and heat shuts things down. Spanish mackerel are a legitimate bonus at the mouth whenever tide is running, and with a strong tidal pull today that opportunity is real. Account for the run time from your launch point and build that into your storm-window planning — you want to be heading back or tucked in somewhere safe well before 1 PM. Slightly stained water argues for a noisy topwater or a chartreuse/white paddle tail to help fish locate the lure in the low-clarity conditions.

rocky.aiNote: Rocky Bayou sits inside Fred Gannon Rocky Bayou State Park near Niceville, offering protected, scenic water that sees significantly less pressure than bayous closer to the 331 Bridge. Freshwater influence from Rocky Creek makes flounder fishing excellent, and glass-calm state park coves are ideal for sight-fishing redfish. Mangrove snapper hold near dock pilings, adding a species option not commonly found at other dashboard locations.
rocky.todaysCall: Rocky Bayou's low-pressure environment and state park setting make it a rewarding destination when conditions allow the run — today's near-calm westerly winds are favorable, but factor in that this is the furthest location on the dashboard and build extra buffer time around the pre-1 PM storm window. Glass-calm coves here are ideal for sight-fishing redfish, and the spring tide push will have fish moving and feeding actively early; get there at first light for the best window before bright sun and 85°F water push fish into shaded or deeper structure. Mangrove snapper near dock pilings are a strong mid-morning option once the sun climbs and topwater action slows — a small live shrimp or cut bait fished tight to pilings is the play. Flounder at the creek mouth remain a structural bet given the freshwater influence from Rocky Creek, though no specific flounder reports are in this week's bay-wide data. The protected coves also serve as a reasonable storm shelter if that small storm chance materializes before your planned departure.
